New wok for the truck, August 2024. The old one warped after Tash quenched it under the tap mid-service. This time I wrote down every step so whoever seasons the next one doesn't have to guess.

## The wok

14 inch hand-hammered carbon steel, round base, from the hardware shelf at Wing Yip on Oldham Road. £24.50. 1.6 mm gauge... no, they said 15 gauge, about 1.8 mm. Steel loop handle plus one long wooden handle. Round base sits in the truck's wok burner (22 kW, Lincat OPUS 800 OG8401). For the flat at home I've got a flat-bottomed 13 inch one from Souschef, £32, which is fine on the induction.

## Getting the factory coating off

They ship it covered in a clear lacquer so it doesn't rust in the shop. If you don't burn this off properly you'll be eating it.

- scrub with hot water, washing-up liquid and a green scourer, 5 min
- on the 22 kW burner, full whack, rotate it so every bit of the inside and outside goes blue, then dull grey-brown
- about 15 min. Stinks. Back doors of the truck open, extractor on max.
- rinse, dry on the burner

## Seasoning, first round

This is where it's NOT like the skillets in [[Cast iron care]]. No oven. Carbon steel is thin, it heats fast and the seasoning goes on over direct flame.

1. medium-high heat, 2 tbsp groundnut oil
2. 150 g sliced ginger, 1 bunch spring onions (green parts) cut in 5 cm lengths
3. stir-fry for 15 min, pushing the aromatics up the sides so the oil coats right up to the lip
4. bin the aromatics, wipe with kitchen roll
5. thin coat of oil, heat until it smokes, let it smoke 1 min, cool
6. repeat step 5 three times

The ginger and spring onion thing is how Mr Chau at Wing Yip said his dad did it. Makes no chemical difference as far as I can tell but it smells right and gets oil in every corner.

## What it looks like

After round one: patchy bronze, some blue, some black near the base. Normal. By week 3 of daily use it's black in the centre and bronze up the sides. The colour is not the point, the non-stick is.

## Daily care on the truck

- rinse hot while the wok is hot, bamboo brush, no soap needed most days
- back on the flame to dry, 30 s
- 1 tsp oil, wipe, smoke briefly
- never leave water in it. Never quench it under a cold tap (RIP old wok, Aug 2024)

## Problems I've had

- sticky brown patches: too much oil left on between services. Burn it off on high for 2 min.
- rust spot after the January layoff (van off 3 weeks, 2025): scourer, then the full seasoning step 5 three more times
- egg welded on during the fried rice test: the wok wasn't hot enough. Needs to smoke before the oil goes in, same as [[Weeknight stir fry]]

## Heat numbers

IR gun readings, 22 kW burner full: centre 380°C at 90 s, lip about 180°C. That gradient is the whole point of a round wok, you push stuff up the side to slow it down. For the [[麻婆豆腐]] I drop to medium, the bean paste burns above about 200°C.

## Cost

Wok £24.50, bamboo brush £2, wooden lid £11. Total £37.50, cheaper than one day's lost sales from a warped pan.
